chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ja'far ibn Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm in the night prayer from the beginning of the night until its end, but the best of that is when the middle of the night arrives."

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: We have clarified the reasoning in similar reports, and the summary is that the time for the night prayer is after the middle of the night until the rising of dawn. What was narrated regarding the concession for advancing it to the beginning of the night is only for the traveler and the sick person, and whoever knows that if he does not pray in the beginning of the night he will be occupied and unable to make it up. As for when the other excuses are removed, it is not permissible according to what we clarified, and that which also confirms this is what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the best time to perform the night prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the general permissibility of Salat al-Layl throughout the night, while highlighting the middle of the night as the peak of virtue. Shaykh al-Tusi’s commentary refines this by distinguishing between the ideal time for the general populace (after midnight) and the concession for travelers or the ill to pray earlier, ensuring the prayer is not missed due to fatigue or sleep. This distinction underscores the Shia jurisprudential balance between spiritual excellence and practical ease.
